Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

be silent verb

also keep quiet, say nothing, hold one’s tongue, keep silent, fall silent, shut up

classical

Cic. Sest. 40: tacendō loquī vidēbantur (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Verr. 1.27: an mē tacitūrum tantīs dē rēbus exīstimāvistis? (Lewis & Short)

taceō, tacēre, tacuī, tacitum

verb, second conjugation

be silent, say nothing; keep quiet about

Not to speak; a narrower word than silēre, to be still, to make no noise (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • sileō, silēre, siluī — be still, make no sound; say nothing of

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Liv. 39.27: optimum quemque silēre (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sull. 80: cum cēterī dē nōbīs silent (Lewis & Short)

    Stronger than tacēre (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • tacendō loquī vidēbantur

    by their silence they seemed to speakCic. Sest. 40 (Lewis & Short)

  • cum cēterī dē nōbīs silent

    when the others say nothing about usCic. Sull. 80 (Lewis & Short)

See also be quiet, silent, silence, quiet!.

SourcesLewis & Short: taceo · Lewis & Short: sileo
